\section[válido]{válido — valid}

\label{lesson:PT-C384-valido}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the offence, then the Portuguese for to transgress.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: válido}
\textbf{válido} — \textquotedblleft{}valid\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O meu passaporte ainda é válido.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{My passport is still valid.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Válido até} — valid until.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{válido} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{validus} \textquotedblleft{}strong, healthy, in good order\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{valēre} \textquotedblleft{}to be strong\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{válido}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{válido}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{válido}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the offence, then the Portuguese for to transgress, then say \emph{válido} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does válido mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Valid\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[caducar]{caducar — to expire, to lapse}

\label{lesson:PT-C384-caducar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to transgress, then the Portuguese for valid.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: caducar}
\textbf{caducar} — \textquotedblleft{}to expire, to lapse\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O cartão caducou no mês passado.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The card expired last month.}
\end{quote}

European Portuguese, of documents; \emph{caducado} — expired.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{caducar} is built on \emph{caduco} \textquotedblleft{}falling, worn out\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from Latin \emph{cadūcus} \textquotedblleft{}falling, perishable\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{cadere} \textquotedblleft{}to fall\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{caducar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{caducar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{caducar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to transgress, then the Portuguese for valid, then say \emph{caducar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does caducar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To expire, to lapse\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[expirar]{expirar — to run out, to expire; to breathe out}

\label{lesson:PT-C384-expirar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for valid, then the Portuguese for to expire.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: expirar}
\textbf{expirar} — \textquotedblleft{}to run out, to expire; to breathe out\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O prazo expira amanhã.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The deadline runs out tomorrow.}
\end{quote}

Also to breathe out: \emph{inspirar e expirar}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{expirar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{exspīrāre} \textquotedblleft{}to breathe out, to expire\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB, Lewis \& Short), built from \emph{ex} and \emph{spīrāre} \textquotedblleft{}to breathe\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{expirar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{expirar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for valid, then the Portuguese for to expire, then say \emph{expirar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does expirar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To run out, to expire; to breathe out\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[renovar]{renovar — to renew; to renovate}

\label{lesson:PT-C384-renovar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to expire, then the Portuguese for to run out.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: renovar}
\textbf{renovar} — \textquotedblleft{}to renew; to renovate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Tenho de renovar o cartão de cidadão.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I have to renew my identity card.}
\end{quote}

Also to renovate a house.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{renovar} comes from Latin \emph{renovāre} \textquotedblleft{}to renew, to restore\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{novus} \textquotedblleft{}new\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[o certificado]{o certificado — the certificate}

\label{lesson:PT-C384-certificado}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to run out, then the Portuguese for to renew.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o certificado}
\textbf{o certificado} — \textquotedblleft{}the certificate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Recebi o certificado no fim do curso.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I received the certificate at the end of my course.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Certificado de habilitações} — certificate of qualifications.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{certificado} is the participle of \emph{certificar}, which is usually traced to Late Latin \emph{certificāre} \textquotedblleft{}to make certain\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{certus} \textquotedblleft{}sure\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to run out, then the Portuguese for to renew, then say \emph{o certificado} again
